The Royal Ring

A king stands above the grass. The frame around him opens onto a far larger performance of power, labour and remembrance.

09
First encounter · The spectacle

What lies beyond a royal photograph?

The original picture records the king and those immediately around him. The wider scene is a research-informed artistic construction, not recovered film.

“The king occupied the howdah; an organised world made the shot possible.”

Begin by looking at the image. When you are ready, reveal the nine places where the historical research changes what you see.

Historical distinction: The original photograph is a reproduction from the Australian National University's Herzog & Higgins album sequence, with the individual camera operator unconfirmed. The colour surroundings and the exact positions of Chandra Shumsher, Adolphus Duke of Teck and Ernest Brooks are artistic interpretations. Brooks is depicted as the photographer by curatorial choice.

Prototype content follows Out of Frame — The Royal Ring, Master Annotation Packet v0.5. The display uses a compressed copy for browser performance; the lossless v1.7 PNG remains the artwork master. External archival links lead to third-party collections; image rights and public exhibition licensing remain under review.
